question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}[{\int }_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\frac{3}{{y}^{2}(1+9{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\frac{3}{(1+(3x)^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)]_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{\pi }{12{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{\pi }{12{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & ={[-\frac{\pi }{12y}]}_{1/3}^{1/4} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{12\cdot \frac{1}{4}}+\frac{\pi }{12\cdot \frac{1}{3}} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$
